prediction.by: user, 2026-11-18, cell P1.27 done_when: 'rules filed first; per-site map S per item, one gain beside it, gaps with spread, update sizes reported; no cut-offs or labels'
prediction.reported: per item (a saved state at its own size, or a larger-side state times E187's c): S, KL(F || M), KL(F || H), H's max relative logit error and each site's fit residual for readings 1, 2 and 3; the update's size ||dW|| / ||W0|| over the 24 matrices and over the 8 MLP matrices. Per pair and reading 3 and 1: the rules below. Per larger-side state: KL(F_c || M) / KL(F_1 || M) / c^2. Reading 2 is in the item files only; no rule reads it
prediction.premise_doubt: a scaled-down update is not a model that learned less: F = M + c dW moves along the same direction, and to first order in the update both KL(F || M) and KL(F || H) scale as c^2, so S does not change with c at leading order. A matched gap equal to the original one therefore says S does not read the length of an update along its own direction; it does not say S would not read a model that learned less

rules.defs: For a pair and reading r: S_orig(side) is the list of that side's items at their own size (c = 1), in E187's state order; S_match(side) the same with the larger side's items times E187's c (the smaller side unchanged). gap_original = mean S_orig(reuse) - mean S_orig(new); gap_matched = mean S_match(reuse) - mean S_match(new). se_original = sqrt(var(S_orig(reuse)) / n_reuse + var(S_orig(new)) / n_new), sample variances (the spread of gap_original over seeds; sides have unequal seed counts, so no per-seed pairing). shift_by_state = S_match - S_orig for each larger-side state (paired: the same state at two sizes); shift_mean its mean, so gap_matched - gap_original = +shift_mean when the reuse side is larger and -shift_mean when the new side is
rules.R1_sign: per pair, readings 3 and 1: 'same' when gap_matched has the sign of gap_original, 'flipped' when the opposite, 'zero' when either is exactly 0
rules.R2_kept: per pair, readings 3 and 1: gap_matched / gap_original (1 = unchanged by matching size, 0 = gone, below 0 = reversed); null when gap_original is exactly 0
rules.R3_shift_within_se: per pair, readings 3 and 1: |shift_mean| <= se_original, true or false. Expected true on every pair under reading 3 (the leading-order argument in premise_doubt); a false names a pair whose survival moved with size by more than its own seed spread
rules.edge_cases: an item missing or with S null (KL(F || M) at or under kl_floor) leaves its pair and reading with {'missing': true} and no rule read. A side with under 2 items gives se_original null and R3 null (none here: every side has 2 to 8 seeds). Ties: R1 'zero' only on an exact 0; every S of a pair equal gives gap 0, R1 'zero', R2 null, se 0 and R3 true (0 <= 0). Do-nothing (c = 0) is never an item of a pair; at c = 1 every shift is 0 by construction, so R1 'same', R2 = 1 and R3 true, the identity reading of the rules. All checked on made-up S before filing (scratch edge_rules.py, 2026-11-18): ties, identity, a raised scaled side, one null item, one missing item, a flipped gap

noise_floor.repro_tol: 1e-4, an eighth of the smallest reading 3 seed spread E197 measured on a pair (0.0008, identity against random table, experiments/held_model_retention/results/summary.json), so a reproduction inside it cannot move a gap's reading
noise_floor.gaps: E197's reading 3 gap seed spreads 0.0008 to 0.0029 over four seeds; se_original is this run's own spread for each pair

blind_to.all: what an update learned beyond its direction (premise_doubt); a size effect that is not a rescale of the same update; anything outside the 512 read windows and the last position
blind_to.reading 3: any change linear in M's activations at a site
blind_to.reading 1: a rule rebuilt as a mix of several M neurons

positive_control: stage 0: do-nothing and the scaled gains-per-block build read their arithmetic values on the scaling path; four unscaled items repeat E197
